data.summary: The 10‑week plan front‑loads the student’s weak units (Kinetics and Equilibrium) while weaving in core content from the other units. Live classes are slotted in their designated weeks, and each week stays within the 6‑hour limit. The final two weeks focus on comprehensive review and timed practice to build stamina for the November AP Chemistry exam.

weeks.focus: Build foundation in atomic structure and periodic trends.
tasks: Read textbook sections for topics 1.1‑1.8 and create a one‑page summary sheet.
Do 15 practice problems on mole calculations and periodic trends, checking answers with the answer key.
Watch a 20‑minute video on electron configuration and write three example configurations.

weeks.focus: Introduce kinetics and attend live class on rate basics.
tasks: Review class notes from live session covering 5.1 and 5.2.
Complete the class worksheet: calculate reaction rates for five given reactions.
Do 10 free‑response FRQs on rate laws, grading with the AP scoring guide.

weeks.focus: Deepen kinetics and start bond fundamentals.
tasks: Solve 8 problems on concentration‑time graphs (5.3) and identify elementary steps (5.4).
Create flashcards for bond types and intramolecular forces (2.1‑2.2).
Write balanced equations for 5 reactions and label bond changes.
Review live class notes on 7.1‑7.3 and complete the provided practice worksheet.
Calculate Q and K for 6 given reactions, deciding direction of shift (7.2).
Do 5 FRQs that require writing equilibrium expressions and determining K (7.4).

weeks.focus: Finish equilibrium and start intermolecular forces.
tasks: Complete a set of 8 problems on equilibrium constant calculations (7.4).
Make a comparison table of intermolecular forces for solids, liquids, gases (3.1‑3.3).
Answer 10 multiple‑choice questions on phase properties, checking explanations.
Solve 12 stoichiometry problems involving net ionic equations (4.1, 4.5).
Draw energy diagrams for exothermic and endothermic reactions (6.1‑6.2).
Complete a worksheet converting between ΔH, q, and temperature changes.

weeks.focus: Acids & bases basics with live class.
tasks: Review class notes on 8.1‑8.2 and answer the class quiz.
Calculate pH and pOH for 6 strong acid/base solutions (8.2).
Do 5 FRQs on weak acid equilibria, using Ka expressions (8.3).

weeks.focus: Complete acid‑base unit and start thermodynamics.
tasks: Write buffer preparation calculations and explain the Henderson‑Hasselbalch equation (8.4).
Solve entropy change problems for 4 processes (9.1‑9.2).
Calculate ΔG for 5 reactions using ΔH and ΔS (9.3).

weeks.focus: Mixed review of all major units.
tasks: Do a 40‑minute mixed‑topic practice set (10 questions from each listed topic).
Create a two‑page master cheat sheet summarizing key equations and concepts.
Review incorrect answers and write a brief explanation for each mistake.

weeks.focus: Timed full‑length practice and final review.
tasks: Take a 90‑minute timed AP practice section covering all units.
Score the section using the official rubric and note areas needing last‑minute review.
Do a 30‑minute rapid‑fire review of any remaining weak spots.

data.final_week_advice: On the day before the exam, relax, review your master cheat sheet, get plenty of sleep, and trust the systematic practice you’ve built over the past ten weeks.
